title: Birbal and the Crow Census of Delhi: Answering the Impossible with Pure Logic
summary: When Emperor Akbar posed an unanswerable question about the exact number of crows residing in the imperial capital, Birbal responded with dazzling mathematical wit.
keywords: Birbal and the Crow Census of the Imperial Capital
full_text:
On a clear morning, Emperor Akbar and Birbal were strolling across the terrace gardens overlooking the Yamuna River. A flock of crows was cawing loudly among the tamarind trees.

Amused by their ceaseless chatter, Akbar turned to Birbal with a teasing challenge:
"Birbal, you claim to have an answer for every enigma in the universe. Tell me: How many crows reside in our imperial capital? I expect an exact census at tomorrow’s court!"

The following morning, the courtiers gathered with suppressed grins, anticipating Birbal’s embarrassment.

Taking the center of the hall, Akbar inquired with mock solemnity:
"Well, Birbal, have you completed the avian census? How many crows dwell within the city walls?"

Birbal bowed with serene confidence:
"Jahanpanah, after meticulous calculation, I can report that there are exactly sixty-seven thousand, four hundred and fifty-two (67,452) crows in the capital."

Akbar raised his eyebrow skeptically:
"And what if a recount by my royal officers reveals that your figure is mistaken?"

Birbal smiled with sparkling innocence:
"If your inspectors count more crows, Jahanpanah, it simply means that visiting relatives from neighboring provinces have arrived to holiday with their cousins in the capital!
And if they count fewer crows, it indicates that our local crows have flown to nearby villages to attend weddings and festivals with their kin!"

The court exploded into laughter, and Akbar shook his head in sheer admiration. Birbal proved that absurd questions are best answered with sparkling wit and playful logic.
